prompt.context: Our client is a disgraced former congressman, Tony Politician, that resigned after numerous indecent text messages he sent surfaced in the media. After congress, Tony is considering using his vast resources to purchase one of three companies. Our job is to ensure he picks the right company that matches his interest and expertise, and is also profitable.
prompt.question: Which of the three companies should Tony purchase? Your evaluation should consider both quantitative and qualitative factors.

clarifying_info.q: Can you tell me more about Tony's background?
clarifying_info.a: Provide Exhibit 1. Tony was born in the Bronx in 1965, first born of 13 kids, graduated from West Point (top of class), served in the Army 8 years, worked at Apple 18 months before being fired for lack of creativity, served in Congress for NYC 2006–2013, and struck it rich prospecting for oil and gas. He is interested in mobile phone security, wants to leave a legacy, loves conspiracy theory movies, and hates the Midwest (particularly Kansas). He is married but divorce proceedings are imminent.

clarifying_info.q: What are the three companies being considered?
clarifying_info.a: PictSecure: a picture-sharing app that ensures pictures cannot be forwarded beyond the original recipient; start-up in Santa Barbara, CA; highly technical product. Doom Shelters: builds and installs Doomsday Shelters (bomb-proof, haz-mat-proof living quarters); mom-and-pop company in Wichita, KS; construction-focused with conspiracy-theory-driven customers. Bossy Pants Cakes: gourmet cake company made famous by a reality show highlighting provocatively themed baked goods; established bakery in Brooklyn, NY; looking to establish online presence and expand to the West Coast.

exhibits.title: Background for Tony Politician
exhibits.shows: A one-page profile of Tony Politician covering personal background, work experience, community service, and personal interests
exhibits.data: Born Bronx 1965; West Point grad (top of class); Army 8 yrs; Apple 18 months (fired); Congress NYC 2006–2013; oil and gas prospector; interests: mobile security, legacy, conspiracy movies; hates Kansas

exhibits.title: Information for Each Firm
exhibits.shows: A financial table comparing PictSecure, Doom Shelters, and Bossy Pants Cakes for 2012 and 2013, with operational and financial line items
exhibits.data: PictSecure 2013: Units Sold 2,666,666; Personnel 16; SG&A/person $125k; COGS/unit $0; Price/unit $3.00; Sales $8.0M; COGS $0; SG&A $2.0M; Taxes $2.0M; Dep $0; CapEx $0; R=20%; g=15%; Mortgage 0.0%; Personal rate 3%. Doom Shelters 2013: Units Sold 400; Personnel 60; SG&A/person $50k; COGS/unit $20k; Price/unit $50k; Sales $20.0M; COGS $8.0M; SG&A $3.0M; Taxes $3.0M; Dep $0.5M; CapEx $1.0M; R=20%; g=10%; Mortgage 3.7%; Personal rate 4%. Bossy Pants Cakes 2013: Units Sold 4,000,000; Personnel 100; SG&A/person $40k; COGS/unit $3.50; Price/unit $7.50; Sales $30.0M; COGS $14.0M; SG&A $4.0M; Taxes $4.0M; Dep $1.0M; CapEx $2.0M; R=15%; g=5%; Mortgage 4.5%; Personal rate 3%. Note: Exhibit also contains 2012 figures and mortgage/personal interest rates which are not needed for the NPV calculation.

framework: Qualitative fit: Assess each company against Tony's personal background, interests, and expertise (technology/security interest, aversion to Kansas, desire for legacy)
Financial analysis: Calculate 2013 Free Cash Flow (FCF = Sales - COGS - SG&A - Taxes + Depreciation - CapEx) for each firm, then NPV using Gordon Growth Model (NPV = FCF / (R - g))
Valuation vs. asking price: Compare NPV to purchase price (NPV - Price) to determine expected value created
Recommendation: Synthesize qualitative fit and financial attractiveness into a final recommendation with risks and mitigants

questions.prompt: Calculate the 2013 Free Cash Flow for each of the three firms.
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply FCF = Sales - COGS - SG&A - Taxes + Depreciation - CapEx using 2013 figures only. Mortgage rates and personal interest rates in the exhibit are distractors and should be ignored. Strong candidates identify and discard irrelevant data quickly.

math.setup: FCF = Sales - (COGS + SG&A) - Taxes + Depreciation - CapEx
math.answer: PictSecure FCF = $4.0M; Doom Shelters FCF = $5.5M; Bossy Pants Cakes FCF = $7.0M

questions.prompt: Calculate the NPV for each firm using the Gordon Growth Model.
questions.guidance: NPV = FCF / (R - g). Candidate should use each firm's respective Rate of Return (R) and Growth (g) from Exhibit 2. Mortgage rates and personal interest rates are distractors.

math.answer: PictSecure NPV = $80M; Doom Shelters NPV = $55M; Bossy Pants Cakes NPV = $70M

questions.prompt: Asking prices are: PictSecure $62M, Doom Shelters $33M, Bossy Pants Cakes $49M. Does this change your recommendation?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute expected value = NPV - Asking Price. PictSecure: $80M - $62M = $18M. Doom Shelters: $55M - $33M = $22M. Bossy Pants Cakes: $70M - $49M = $21M. Financially, Doom Shelters offers the highest expected value ($22M), but Tony hates Kansas and the Midwest. This is intentionally ambiguous — a strong candidate defends their position with clear logic, acknowledging the financial advantage of Doom Shelters while making a reasoned argument for or against it based on qualitative fit.

math.answer: Doom Shelters highest at $22M; Bossy Pants Cakes $21M; PictSecure $18M

recommendation: PictSecure is the primary recommendation: it aligns with Tony's passion for mobile security technology, leverages his tech interest, and his own scandal is a compelling authentic selling point for a product designed to secure pictures
PictSecure has the highest standalone NPV at $80M, and Tony's background at Apple (even if brief) and his personal interest in mobile security give him relevant operating credibility
If pressed on financials alone, Doom Shelters offers $22M expected value vs. PictSecure's $18M, but Tony explicitly hates Kansas and the Midwest, making a Wichita-based company a poor qualitative fit
risks: PictSecure's high assumed growth rate of 15% may not materialize — if growth slows, NPV drops sharply
Tony has no prior experience running a company independently; operational execution risk is high
His public scandal could create PR challenges for any acquisition, especially a consumer-facing brand
PictSecure is a startup with a small team of 16 — scaling rapidly while maintaining product quality is difficult
next_steps: Conduct due diligence on PictSecure's technology IP, user traction, and competitive moat
Assess management team quality and retention risk post-acquisition
Model downside NPV scenarios with lower growth rates
Develop a PR strategy leveraging Tony's scandal as authentic product endorsement
